byteward.title: Version 2.0 of the Brindle programming language is released
byteward.author: Dana Whitlock
body: [f01: Version 2.0 of Brindle, the open-source programming language, was released on Sunday.] [f04: It's the language's first major release since 2022.]

[f03: Brindle's maintainers say the new version compiles code up to 40% faster than Brindle 1.9.] [f02: The release also adds an official package manager.] That alone may win over developers who found setting up a project a chore.
[f05: Brindle 1 will keep getting security fixes until June 2028.] That gives teams with large codebases time to plan the move, and they'll probably need it.

ohm-and-bit.title: Brindle 2.0 programming language released
ohm-and-bit.author: Imogen Vale
body: [f03: The headline number in Brindle 2.0 is compile speed: up to 40 percent faster than version 1.9.] [f06: Most of that comes from a new incremental compiler, which reuses work from earlier builds instead of starting from scratch.]
[f09: Compiled programs also come out about 15 percent smaller.] Smaller programs load faster and take less space, which matters more than it sounds for software that runs on small devices.

The cost is compatibility. [f07: Code written with the old async syntax has to be updated.] [f08: A migration tool handles about 90 percent of that work automatically, according to the maintainers.] The remaining tenth is where teams will spend their time.
